story.title: Tour
story.welcome.title: A traffic twin for any city
story.welcome.text: TrafficTwin shows a city's traffic, forecasts it and simulates it. It works for any city built from OpenStreetMap; this one is the city in the switcher. Every value on screen says whether it is real, recorded or simulated.
story.trip.title: A trip across the city
story.trip.text: Choose where you start and where you are going, or click the map. The route runs on the city's own roads; a colour means traffic data exists there, grey means none.
story.recorded.title: A recorded day
story.recorded.text: Where a published recording exists, 'Recorded day' colours the road with what was measured on that day. It is real, but it is not today.
story.city3d.title: The city in 3D
story.city3d.text: Roads and buildings are real map data; the vehicles are simulated. The note above the map says what the simulation was matched to.
story.ambulance.title: An ambulance, warned ahead
story.ambulance.text: Start one ambulance and watch vehicles and traffic lights react to its alert. This is one run to watch, not a result; the sentence above it comes from the full ambulance study on Research.
story.emergency.title: What the alert saves, and what it doesn't
story.emergency.text: One sentence from the ambulance study: what warning nearby vehicles saved, how reliably, and what smarter traffic lights saved, at the traffic level it names. 'How we know' opens the full study. The city's emergency numbers are shown, never dialled.
story.offline.title: When the network is down
story.offline.text: Messages can travel from phone to phone as vehicles meet. The sentence says what our simulation delivered and why few were reached.
story.addCity.title: Any city in the world
story.addCity.text: Type a name, place the small area to simulate, build it from OpenStreetMap. It appears in the switcher and in 3D.
story.research.title: How we know
story.research.text: Every table, source and caveat lives here. The rule: no number without a saved run, and nothing from one city shown as another's. The tour ends here.
shell.cityListFailed: The city list could not be loaded ({why}). The server may be an old copy or still starting.

lab.ev.measured: Measured in a traffic simulation of a congested Los Angeles corridor (real road network, real detector data feeding the forecast) with the same vehicles and journeys in every world. Only the routing advice changed.
lab.ev.arm.oracleSub: total travel time vs reactive routing
lab.ev.arm.forecastNone: The AI forecast vs no advice
lab.ev.today: What the AI forecast does today
lab.ev.todayYes: The learned forecast beats both no advice and reactive routing on unseen days.
lab.ev.todayNo: The Graph WaveNet forecast is validated on real Los Angeles detector data (it beats "traffic stays the same"), and routing on it is {gVr} against reactive routing ({gVrWord}). But against no advice at all it is {gVb} ({gVbWord}), and a shuffled forecast used as a control scores {rnd} vs reactive ({rndWord}). So the gain over reactive routing comes from the disciplined V2X advice pipeline, not yet from forecast skill. We say so rather than round it up.
lab.ev.why: Why perfect information helps and the forecast does not yet: the forecast prices only the roads with sensors; the perfect-information arm prices every road. Covering more roads is the next step.
lab.ev.ownNames: The labels in English below are the experiment's own names, as written in its run files.
lab.ev.means1: only changes your route when the predicted saving is worth it, and only for a budgeted share of drivers per round — the discipline that beat reactive routing here.
lab.ev.means2: steers advice only where a model has been validated on that city's own road data; elsewhere routes follow current traffic.
lab.ev.means3: the app routes on the project's own road network with the last recorded traffic when no live provider is available, and says so on screen.
lab.ev.how1: Demand was raised on a real Los Angeles corridor until the roads were congested but stable (rule frozen before any result: travel-time index ≥ 1.3, standing jams, ≤ 1 % lost vehicles).
lab.ev.how2: Every world started from one saved simulation state. First the perfect-information arm had to beat reactive routing; only then were the learned forecasts tested.
lab.ev.how3: Only 30 % of drivers are connected, as in real life; messages travel through a simulated V2X channel with latency, loss and expiry.
lab.ev.how4: A result counts only when it held across all unseen days (paired 95 % confidence interval), never on a lucky one. A shuffled forecast runs as a negative control.
lab.ev.congestedSub: demand is synthetic (scaled random trips on the real road network); the METR-LA data carries no traffic counts, so it is never called real traffic
lab.ev.statusSub: computed by the backend from run files ({files}); no page or document may set a status by hand
lab.ev.lowLoad: The earlier low-load experiment is kept as a negative result:
lab.ev.verdict.yes: Yes — routing on the AI forecast makes trips
lab.ev.verdict.future: Knowing the future helps — a perfect view of the next hour cuts total travel time
lab.ev.verdict.futureStrong: {pct} % against reactive routing. Today's AI forecast does not yet capture that gain.
lab.ev.verdict.no: Not yet — in this test, no information source beat reactive routing with confidence.

lab.rq1.title: Forecasting: how far ahead, and why Dhaka differs (RQ1)
lab.rq1.sub: Speed forecasts 15, 30 and 60 minutes ahead on Los Angeles and San Francisco Bay Area loop detectors and on Dhaka's camera sites; baselines, zero-shot foundation models and our trained models.
lab.rq1.none: RQ1 has not been run yet.
lab.rq1.findLab: {city} ({ds}): at 60 minutes the best is {best} at {v} mph mean absolute error, against {p} for persistence; the best zero-shot model is {f} at {fv}.
lab.rq1.findDhaka: Dhaka (DhaTraX, three camera sites, one day each), the best model other than persistence: at 15 minutes {b15} {v15} km/h against persistence {p15}; at 30 minutes {b30} {v30} against {p30}; at 60 minutes {b60} {v60} against {p60}.
lab.rq1.findUnseen: Unseen city: XGBoost trained in Los Angeles and run unchanged in the San Francisco Bay Area scores {moved} mph at 60 minutes, against {home} when trained there; moving cities costs {cost} %. The six graph models cannot move at all.
lab.rq1.whyText: Dhaka's speeds jump: {sg0}-{sg1} % of 5-minute steps change by more than 30 % of free-flow, against {sgLa} % on a median Los Angeles sensor-day and {sgBay} % in the Bay Area. {cvMore} of {n} sites vary more than a median Los Angeles sensor-day (coefficient of variation {cvSites} against {cvLa}, and {cvBay} in the Bay Area); {aLess} of {n} remember less an hour ahead (autocorrelation at 60 minutes {a0}-{a1} against {aLa} and {aBay}). So what a model learns from Los Angeles's smooth roads does not carry: XGBoost trained on METR-LA is {dkCost} % worse than persistence in Dhaka at 60 minutes, while moving it to the Bay Area costs {cost} %. And the models that win in Los Angeles ({best} {bv} against persistence {pv} at 60 minutes) learned months of each sensor's history; a Dhaka camera site has one recorded day, so there is nothing to train them on, and only zero-shot models can be used.

lab.rq2.title: Ambulance alert: how far it helps (RQ2)
lab.rq2.sub: Time the ambulance saves against a siren-only run of the same seed and density, from light traffic to gridlock, by the share of vehicles that receive the alert; Q-learning signals (sumo-rl) as a stronger signal baseline.
lab.rq2.none: RQ2 has not been run yet.
lab.rq2.findDensity: With every vehicle equipped, the alert's median saving is {list}.
lab.rq2.findStops: The alert stops saving {pct} % or more at demand x{scale}, whatever share of vehicles is equipped.
lab.rq2.findAlways: The alert saves {pct} % or more at every density run, with enough vehicles equipped.
lab.rq2.findRl: Q-learning signals without the alert: median saving {list} against SUMO's own signal programmes (the 3 signals near the route).
lab.rq2.findDhakaReached: Dhaka's recorded density at the INT camera ({rec} vehicles/km, 07:00-08:00) is matched closest by demand x{scale} ({sim} vehicles/km).
lab.rq2.findDhakaNot: Dhaka's recorded density at the INT camera ({rec} vehicles/km, 07:00-08:00) is not reached before the simulation gridlocks: the densest run gives {sim} vehicles/km on that section.
lab.rq2.whyText: Time saved {wRel} the free width ahead of the ambulance in the siren-only run (Spearman rho {rho}, 95 % CI {lo} to {hi}, {runs} paired runs) and {qRel} the queue at the route's signals (rho {qrho}, CI {qlo} to {qhi}).
lab.rq2.tableTitle: Median time saved against the siren-only run (paired by seed; % of that trip), by demand
lab.rq2.fig.rq2_density: Time saved against traffic density, per arm
lab.rq2.fig.rq2_share: Time saved against the share of vehicles alerted, per density
lab.rq2.fig.rq2_why: Time saved against free space ahead and queues at signals
lab.rq2.findSlower: In {worse} of {runs} alert runs the ambulance was more than 5 s slower than with the siren alone; these runs stay in every mean.
lab.rq2.whyYield: It {yRel} the share of alerted vehicles that actually moved aside (rho {rho}, CI {lo} to {hi}).
lab.rq2.gap: Why the simulation stays far below Dhaka's recorded density at the INT camera ({recorded_veh_km} vehicles/km, 07:00-08:00): not the definition (both count every vehicle class on the whole road over about 90 m); not the space per vehicle (SUMO's lengths and gaps allow about {jam_density_veh_km} vehicles/km on those 3 lanes, and other roads reach {elsewhere_peak_veh_km} at gridlock); partly lane discipline (smaller lateral gaps for two-wheelers, rickshaws and CNGs raise the section's mean from {sim_mean_veh_km} to {tight_mean_veh_km}); mainly supply (only {sim_entered_veh_h} vehicles an hour enter the section, against {recorded_flow_veh_h} recorded, and the network gridlocks elsewhere first). So these ambulance results come from a simulation that does not reach Dhaka's recorded density on that road.
lab.rq2.findHelpAt: A median saving of {pct} % or more is reached only at demand {list}.
lab.rq2.findHelpNot: At demand {list} no equipped share reaches it.
lab.rq2.findHelpNone: No equipped share reaches a median saving of {pct} % at any density.
lab.rq2.whyBlocked: It {bRel} how long the siren-only ambulance stood blocked (rho {rho}, CI {lo} to {hi}).
lab.rq2.whyRoom: The free width ahead hardly changes with density ({lo}-{hi} m over all levels): on this route there is room to move aside at every level, so room is not what limits the alert.
lab.rq2.whySignals: Smarter signals do more: the Q-learning signals' median saving beats the alert to every vehicle at {beats} of {of} densities, which suggests the ambulance's delay on this route sits at the junctions more than behind vehicles that could move aside.
lab.rq2.findCorridor.dhaka: At the density the corridor reaches ({sim} vehicles/km on the INT section against the recorded {rec}), the time the alert to every vehicle saves is a median {alert} (a minus means later than the siren alone), over {seeds} paired seeds; {slower} of them were slower than the siren alone.
lab.rq2.findCorridor.corridor: The corridor reaches {sim} vehicles/km on the INT section, outside the recorded range around {rec}, so this row is not Dhaka's density. There the time the alert to every vehicle saves is a median {alert} (a minus means later than the siren alone), over {seeds} paired seeds; {slower} of them were slower than the siren alone.
lab.rq2.findCorridorFlow: Only {flow} vehicles an hour pass the section there, against {rec} recorded: the density matches, the flow does not.
lab.rq2.gapCorridor: Supply tested: a corridor around the route, loaded with the recorded counts and the smaller lateral gaps, overshoots at the full counts ({corridor_full_veh_km} vehicles/km) and reaches {corridor_veh_km} vehicles/km at x{corridor_scale} of the counts, inside the recorded range ({q25}-{q75}); but only {corridor_flow_veh_h} vehicles an hour pass, against {recorded_flow_veh_h} recorded. The density is reached; the recorded flow at that density is not.

lab.rq2.whyDhaka: At the Dhaka-density level, time saved {wRel} the free width ahead (rho {rho}, 95 % CI {lo} to {hi}, {runs} paired runs), {qRel} the queue at the route's signals (rho {qrho}) and {bRel} how long the siren-only ambulance stood blocked (rho {brho}; median {blocked} s blocked). Free width ahead averages {fw} m there.
lab.rq2.dhakaCause: Why the alert slows the ambulance at Dhaka density (inspected run by run): in the {slow} of {runs} slower runs the ambulance stood {stood} s in all; {share} % of that time it was held by a chain of vehicles ending at an alerted vehicle waiting at the end of a lane it needed to leave. The make-way rule forbids that vehicle's own lane change until the ambulance passes, and the ambulance cannot pass, so both wait until SUMO teleports the vehicle after 300 s: a simulation artefact, not observed driver behaviour. Letting alerted vehicles keep their own lane changes gives a median saving of {sMed} s (25-75 %: {sLo} to {sHi} s; {sSlow} of {sRuns} slower, {sCrash} crashed); alerting only vehicles within 50 m ahead gives {nMed} s ({nLo} to {nHi} s; {nSlow} of {nRuns} slower); keeping junctions free of make-way changes nothing ({jMed} s). The other {rest} % of the standing time is not explained. Ten seeds at one density: whether the alert helps at Dhaka density is not known.
plain.amb.laterUnknown: made the ambulance about {s} s later on a {trip} s trip in our simulation, and we do not yet know why
lab.rq2.v1Label: Earlier rule (make-way v1), kept as a record:
lab.rq2.makeway: How alerted vehicles move aside in these results (make-way v2): they keep their own route lane changes, and only those within {d} m ahead of the ambulance move aside. No published distance for an electronic alert exists, so 50 m and 100 m were piloted and chosen by a rule fixed beforehand, amended once by the owner after the pilot; time saved was not used. The earlier rule held every alerted vehicle up to 1,000 m ahead until the ambulance passed, which created the circular wait described below.
lab.rq2.qlearning: Q-learning signals at Dhaka density, inspected run by run: on the {seeds} seeds where they made the ambulance slower, it stood {stood} s in all (siren alone on the same seeds: {siren} s); {near} of those seconds were within 100 m of a traffic light. The next light on its route was green for it in {green} s, red in {red} s, and none was left ahead in {none} s. The queues it stood in were short (median {head} vehicles to the head) and their heads were not at a light; many ended at a vehicle waiting to change lane. So the lights did not hold the ambulance directly; the cause of this slowdown is not established.
lab.rq2.ovnTitle: Old rule (make-way v1, artefact) against the corrected rule (v2): median time saved (25-75 %); runs slower than the siren alone

lab.nav.live-twin.label: Live twin
lab.nav.live-twin.hint: A running simulation of the corridor: place a crash or an ambulance and watch three forecasters learn
liveTwin.intro: A SUMO simulation of the city's corridor that keeps running, computed now on this server. Every simulated minute the corridor's detectors give each road's speed to three forecasters side by side: an online model that learns from each new value (River), Chronos-Bolt zero-shot, and "no change". RQ1's graph models are not used: they are tied to METR-LA's 207 sensors and cannot run on these roads.

liveTwin.mode.ambulance_to: starts an ambulance: first click the start, then the destination
liveTwin.signals: Signals: SUMO's fixed-time programs; the ambulance's route signals turn green when its alert reaches them. Q-learning signals (sumo-rl) run as a separate simulation (main map → Simulation → Smart signals): sumo-rl needs NumPy below 2 and starts its own SUMO, so it cannot share this one.
liveTwin.noAmbulance: None yet: choose an ambulance click and click a road.
liveTwin.fcHow: {roads} roads, {loops} detectors. Every simulated minute each forecaster predicts each road's speed 15 minutes ahead; a prediction is scored when its true value arrives, on the road-minutes all three predicted. The online model starts as "no change" and learns the change from each true value.
